Notification of an Emergency Authorisation
 
1. Member State, and MS notification number
 
ES - ES-2026-38
 
2. In case of repeated derogation: no. of previous derogation(s)
 
1
 
3. Names of active substances
 
Acetamiprid 200.0 g/kg
 
4. Trade name of Plant Protection Product
 
ZUXION GAZEL PLUS SG
 
5. Formulation type
 
SG - Water soluble granules
 
6. Authorisation holder
 
Dirección General de la Producción Agrícola y Ganadera de la Junta de Andalucía
 
7. Time period for authorisation
 
2026-07-15 - 2026-11-11
 
8. Area permitted to be treated
 
 
9. Area actually treated
 
 
10. Further limitations
 
Validity of the authorization: • Andalucia and Murcia: from July 15 to November 11, 2026. • Aragón and Castilla-La Mancha: 
from July 17 to November 11, 2026. • Valencia: from July 24 to November 11, 2026.
 
11. Value of tMRL if needed, including information on the measures taken in order to confine the commodities resulting from 
the treated crop to the territory of the notifying MS pending the setting of a tMRL on the EU level. (PRIMO EFSA model to be 
attached)
 
The requested cultivation practice is the same one that is currently authorized. However, the third application subject to 
exceptional authorization may only be made after collection.

 
12. Validated analytical method for monitoring of residues in plants and plant products.
 
It is not necessary
 
13. Function of the product
(E.g. systemic long acting insecticide; foliar fungicide, used for regular control, elimination scenario etc)
 
insecticide
 
14. Type of danger to plant production or ecosystem
(Provide reasoning for what category the 120 day authorisation is given: quarantine pest; emergent pest, either invading non-
native, or native; emerging resistance in a pest, etc. Whereas reference to the EU quarantine legislation may suffice for 
quarantine pests elaborate reasoning should be provided for the category 'any harmful pest')
 
The big-headed worm (Capnodis tenebrionis) is one of the main pests that affects almond, peach and nectarine crops in our 
autonomous community. The biological cycle of this pest makes it necessary to carry out treatments for its control in spring, at 
which time the wintering adults appear, and in summer, at which time the new adults emerge. They cause damage to the leaves 
and shoots, where bites can be observed. On the other hand, it is also necessary to control larvae in spring, they feed on the roots 
causing the weakening of the trees and frequently causing their death.
 
15. Size and effect of danger
(Describe shortly the area affected, the development over time of the infestation, and the agronomic and economic effects it has)
 
The autonomous community of Andalusia is the main producer of almonds nationwide, with a cultivation area of 238.441 ha, 
according to the 2022 Yearbook of Agricultural and Fisheries Statistics, cultivation that is carried out mainly in dry land. 
According to the same source, the area of peach and nectarine crops in the same year was 2368 ha and 1584 ha, respectively.
 
16. Absence of any other reasonable means
(Describe the alternative control measures (chemical, non-chemical and cultural) and indicate why they do not (in combination) 
suffice. Describe which, if any, authorisations for the pest to be controlled exist in other Member States.
 
Added to the persistent drought in Andalusia is the absence of systemic phytosanitary products that act by contact and ingestion, 
such as those composed of the active substances imidacloprid or thiacloprid. Consequently, the control of the pest has become 
more difficult. Consulting the Official Register of Phytosanitary Products and Material, it has been verified that at this time it is 
only possible to make two applications of acetamiprid for the control of adults of this pest. As a general rule, one of these 
applications is being used, according to the sector, to control other important pests for these crops, such as aphids. Consequently, 
in practice, only a single application is available to cover the next emergence period of bighead worm adults, which is between 
mid-August and the end of September. On the other hand, indicate that the active substance chlorantraniliprole is also authorized 
for the control of Coleoptera in the indicated crops. However, it presents a limited efficacy in the control of adults, in accordance 
with the test entitled: "Control of Big- headed Worm (Capnodis tenebrionis L.) by means of phytosanitary treatments.", which is 
attached as Annex No. 1. For For its part, the substance acetamiptrid is highly effective in controlling adults of this pest, according 
to the same trial. Likewise, it should be noted that there is no active substance authorized for the control of larvae. Consequently, 
it is only possible to carry out applications for the control of adults, which makes it extremely difficult to control the pest once it is 
installed in the cultivation plot.
 
17. Rationale
(Reason the risk management decision based on the findings of 15 to 18, containing especially a description of measures taken to 
ensure consumer protection).
 
The producing sector, represented by Asociafruit and ASAJA Andalucia, has expressed to this General Directorate the need to use 
the active substance acetamiprid 20% in a third application for the control of the big- headed worm in peach, nectarine and 
almond plantations , as the only effective means to fight against this plague An exceedance of the current MRL for peach, 
nectarine and almond is not expected. The proposed uses of acetamiprid do not represent unacceptable acute and chronic risks for 
the consumer.

 
18. Mitigation measures
(Describe what mitigation measures are taken if needed for minimising risk to humans, animals, and the environment, attach 
summary risk assessment. Describe what measures are taken to limit and control use)
 
The requested cultivation practice is the same one that is currently authorized. However, the third application subject to 
exceptional authorization may only be made after collection.
 
19. Applications in progress
(The use notified may have been applied for already, or a suitable alternative PPP may be in the process of authorisation. 
Describe such applications, including a possible date of authorisation)
 
There is no request in progress.
 
20. Research activities
(Describe the research efforts undertaken and/or in progress, their aims, their funding, and their expected date of results. This is 
needed for all categories of dangers, except quarantine pests that can still be eliminated, or infrequent pests, for which no official 
application for a normal authorisation or extension of use of the plant protection product exists. In case of a repeated 
notification: indicate the state of works of the research projects.)
 
It is unknown

SECRETARÍA GENERAL DE RECURSOS AGRARIOS Y 
SEGURIDAD ALIMENTARIA 
 
 
RESOLUCIÓN DE AUTORIZACIÓN EXCEPCIONAL PARA LA COMERCIALIZACIÓN Y 
EL USO DE LOS PRODUCTOS FITOSANITARIOS FORMULADOS A BASE DE 
ACETAMIPRID 20% [SG] P/P PARA EL CONTROL DE GUSANO CABEZUDO EN LOS 
CULTIVOS DEL MELOCOTONERO, NECTARINO Y ALMENDRO 
 
ANTECEDENTES 
 
 El gusano cabezudo (Capnodis tenebrionis) es una de las principales plagas que 
afecta a los cultivos del almendro, melocotonero y nectarino. El ciclo biológico de esta plaga 
hace necesario la realización de tratamientos para su control en primavera, momento en el 
cual aparecen los adultos invernantes, y en verano, momento en el que emergen los nuevos 
adultos. Los adultos provocan daños en las hojas y brotes, donde se pueden observar 
mordeduras. Las larvas se alimentan de las raíces causando el debilitamiento de los árboles 
y provocando con frecuencia la muerte de los mismos. 
 
La incidencia de la plaga es mayor en plantaciones de secano, ya que la humedad 
del suelo actúa como un factor limitante al provocar la muerte de los huevos y de las larvas 
neonatas. Las altas temperaturas registradas en las últimas semanas han provocado una 
rápida evaporación de la humedad acumulada en el suelo. Estas condiciones, crean un 
ambiente especialmente favorable para el desarrollo y proliferación de la plaga, cuyas larvas 
permanecen activas en el interior de las raíces, protegidas de las condiciones superficiales.  
 
A lo dicho anteriormente, se suma la falta de productos fitosanitarios registrados 
sistémicos con acción por contacto e ingestión. 
 
Por todo lo dicho anteriormente, las Comunidades autónomas indicadas en el anexo 
adjunto, desde sus Direcciones Generales correspondientes, han solicitado la autorización 
excepcional de una tercera aplicación post cosecha de los productos fitosanitarios 
autorizados en el Registro Oficial de Productos Fitosanitarios, formulados a base de 
acetamiprid 20% [SG] P/P que están autorizados en el melocotonero (se incluye nectarino) 
o almendro. 
 
FUNDAMENTOS DE DERECHO 
 
I.- Que esta Dirección General es competente para la resolución de la solicitud, de 
conformidad con lo previsto en el artículo 7 del Real Decreto 971/2014, de 21 de noviembre, 
por el que se regula el procedimiento de evaluación de productos fitosanitarios, en relación 
con el artículo 4 del Real Decreto 717/2024, de 23 de julio, por el que se desarrolla la 
estructura orgánica básica del Ministerio de Agricultura, Pesca y Alimentación. 
 
II.- Que el artículo 53 del Reglamento (CE) nº 1107/2009 del Parlamento Europeo y del 
Consejo, de 20 de octubre de 2009, relativo a la comercialización de productos fitosanitarios 
y por el que se derogan las Directivas 79/117/CEE y 91/414/CEE del Consejo establece que, 
en circunstancias especiales, un Estado miembro podría autorizar, por un periodo no 
superior a 120 días, la comercialización de productos fitosanitarios para su utilización 
controlada y limitada, si tal medida fuera necesaria debido a un peligro que no pueda 
controlarse por otros medios razonables.

III.- Que el artículo 34 de la Ley 43/2002, de 20 de noviembre, de sanidad vegetal, establece 
la posibilidad de que el Ministerio de Agricultura, Pesca y Alimentación conceda 
autorizaciones excepcionales de un producto fitosanitario en caso de peligro imprevisible 
que no pueda ser controlado por otros medios.  
 
Por todo lo expuesto y, ante la excepcionalidad de la situación, RESUELVO: 
 
PRIMERO.- Autorizar excepcionalmente los productos fitosanitarios formulados a base de 
acetamiprid 20% [SG] P/P autorizados en el Registro Oficial de Productos Fitosanitarios del 
MAPA en melocotonero (incluye nectarino) o almendro una tercera aplicación para su uso 
contra gusano cabezudo, en las condiciones y Comunidades autónomas que se indican en 
el anexo adjunto y únicamente por el plazo establecido en el punto segundo, para una 
utilización controlada y limitada. 
 
SEGUNDO.- La autorización tendrá vigencia desde el 15 de julio hasta el 11 de noviembre 
de 2026. 
 
TERCERO.- Los tratamientos deberán ser efectuados bajo el control de las autoridades 
competentes de las Comunidades autónomas indicadas en el Anexo adjunto. Además, esta 
autoridad, deberá establecer mecanismos de inspección, vigilancia, control y sanción con el 
fin de asegurar una reducción al mínimo de los posibles riesgos que puedan surgir como 
consecuencia de la aplicación de los productos fitosanitarios autorizados. 
 
CUMPLASE Y NOTIFIQUESE a las Comunidades autónomas y a los titulares de los 
formulados referenciados y dese traslado a la Comisión Europea, conforme al artículo 53 del 
Reglamento (CE) nº 1107/2009. 
 
 
La presente resolución no agota la vía administrativa, y contra ella podrá recurrirse, en 
alzada, ante el Sr. Secretario General de Agricultura y Alimentación, en el plazo de un mes, 
contado a partir del día siguiente a aquel en que tenga lugar su notificación, de acuerdo a lo 
establecido en los artículos 121 y concordantes de la Ley 39/2015, de 1 de octubre, del 
Procedimiento Administrativo Común de las Administraciones Públicas. 
 
 
Firmado electrónicamente por, 
EL DIRECTOR GENERAL 
Emilio Luis García Muro

ANEXO 
 
CONDICIONES DE USO: 
 
- Productos fitosanitarios formulados a base de acetamiprid 20% [SG] P/P que están 
autorizados en el Registro Oficial de Productos Fitosanitarios del MAPA en los cultivos 
de melocotonero (incluye nectarino) o almendro, autorizados únicamente en la 
Comunidad Autónoma de Andalucía. 
- Cultivos: Melocotonero, nectarino, almendro 
- Plaga/enfermedad: Gusano cabezudo (Capnodis tenebrionis) 
- Dosis máxima: 0,25 Kg/ha 
- Nº aplicaciones: Tercera dosis adicional para aplicar después de la recolección del 
fruto. 
- Volumen de caldo: 1000-1500 L/ha 
- Aplicación: Pulverización foliar. 
- Plazo de seguridad: No procede. 
- Efectos de la autorización: Desde el 15 de julio hasta el 11 de noviembre de 2026. 
 
Restricciones: La tercera aplicación tendrá que ser realizada después de la 
recolección del fruto. 
 
 
Nota: En la etiqueta se darán las instrucciones específicas para su correcto uso y las 
advertencias sobre incompatibilidad con otros productos fitosanitarios.

RESOLUCIÓN DE 15 DE JULIO DE 2026 POR LA QUE SE MODIFICA LA RESOLUCIÓN 
DE AUTORIZACIÓN EXCEPCIONAL DE 10 DE JULIO DE 2026 PARA LA 
COMERCIALIZACIÓN Y EL USO DE LOS PRODUCTOS FITOSANITARIOS 
FORMULADOS A BASE DE ACETAMIPRID 20%  [SG] P/P PARA EL CONTROL DE 
GUSANO CABEZUDO EN LOS CULTIVOS DEL MELOCOTONERO, NECTARINO Y 
ALMENDRO 
 
 
ANTECEDENTES 
 
- Resolución de Autorización Excepcional de 10 de julio de 2026 para la 
comercialización y el uso de los productos fitosanitarios formulados a base de acetamiprid 
20% [SG] P/P para el control de gusano cabezudo en los cultivos del melocotonero, nectarino

records.fullText:
Notification of an Emergency Authorisation
 
1. Member State, and MS notification number
 
ES - ES-2026-33
 
2. In case of repeated derogation: no. of previous derogation(s)
 
0
 
3. Names of active substances
 
Hexythiazox 258.7 g/l
 
4. Trade name of Plant Protection Product
 
DIABLO MAX JALISCO SC
 
5. Formulation type
 
SC - Suspension concentrate (= flowable concentrate)
 
6. Authorisation holder
 
Dirección General Agricultura y Ganadería de la Junta de Extremadura
 
7. Time period for authorisation
 
2026-06-09 - 2026-09-28
 
8. Area permitted to be treated
 
 
9. Area actually treated
 
 
10. Further limitations
 
Area permitted to be treated: Autonomous Community of Extremadura: Province of Cáceres: Comarca del Valle del Jerte, 
comarca de la Vera, comarca del Alagón, comarca de Gata, comarca de las Hurdes, comarca de Villuercas y comarca del Ambroz 
and Autonomous Communities of Aragón and Andalucía. Cherry tree authorized in Autonomous Communities of Extremadura 
and Aragón. Almond tree authorized in Autonomous Community of Andalucia. Authorization period:  Extremadura: From June 9 
to September 28, 2026  Aragón: From June 23 to September 20, 2026  Andalucía: From August 17 to November 30, 2026
 
11. Value of tMRL if needed, including information on the measures taken in order to confine the commodities resulting from 
the treated crop to the territory of the notifying MS pending the setting of a tMRL on the EU level. (PRIMO EFSA model to be 
attached)

 
Not applicable.
 
12. Validated analytical method for monitoring of residues in plants and plant products.
 
Not applicable.
 
13. Function of the product
(E.g. systemic long acting insecticide; foliar fungicide, used for regular control, elimination scenario etc)
 
acaricide
 
14. Type of danger to plant production or ecosystem
(Provide reasoning for what category the 120 day authorisation is given: quarantine pest; emergent pest, either invading non-
native, or native; emerging resistance in a pest, etc. Whereas reference to the EU quarantine legislation may suffice for 
quarantine pests elaborate reasoning should be provided for the category 'any harmful pest')
 
Red spider mite (Tetranychus ssp) is considered to be one of the most important pests on many crops, including cherry trees. Lack 
of control means that the main danger is that they weaken the leaf mass, to the point of drying out the plant. Plant necrosis and the 
formation of spider webs. The final effect is a very high decrease in the production and yield of the crop.
 
15. Size and effect of danger
(Describe shortly the area affected, the development over time of the infestation, and the agronomic and economic effects it has)
 
From an economic and social point of view, cherry tree cultivation has a very important social and economic impact in 
Extremadura, with an approximate cultivation area of 9,702 hectares (depending on the year); representing about 36% of the total 
cherry grown in Spain. The damage they cause is weakening the plant and the final effect is a decrease in the production and yield 
of the crop.
 
16. Absence of any other reasonable means
(Describe the alternative control measures (chemical, non-chemical and cultural) and indicate why they do not (in combination) 
suffice. Describe which, if any, authorisations for the pest to be controlled exist in other Member States.
 
There are only 3 registered formulations for the control of mites in cherry trees, all of which are based on hexythiazox, including 
the formulation proposed for this application. All of them are authorized for use before fruit set (BBCH 69). There are no 
registered formulations authorized for post-harvest use. The lack of authorized cherry three products during post-harvest requires 
DIABLO MAX’s exceptional authorization.
 
17. Rationale
(Reason the risk management decision based on the findings of 15 to 18, containing especially a description of measures taken to 
ensure consumer protection).
 
We should take into consideration the biology and phenology of mites and spiders: they initially appear in small pockets and 
develop depending on weather conditions. The incidence of tetranychid mites is higher in dry years, with low rainfall and low 
relative humidity, as well as warm temperatures. Unfortunately, in recent years, under our growing conditions, the climatic trend 
has been precisely this, creating the need to deal with the problems caused by the pest during the post-harvest period. For the 
reason described above, we consider that the use of the DIABLO MAX formulation on this crop, for the control of mites, is in the 
public interest and is of vital importance to the entire affected agricultural sector. Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/1305 of 2 
July 2025 amending Annexes II, III and IV to Regulation (EC) No 396/2005 of the European Parliament and of the Council as 
regards maximum residue limits for hexitiazox in certain products.
 
18. Mitigation measures
(Describe what mitigation measures are taken if needed for minimising risk to humans, animals, and the environment, attach 
summary risk assessment. Describe what measures are taken to limit and control use)
 

It is not considered necessary to adopt any special measures other than those established on the commercial label of the product, 
which is already registered in several Member States in the EU, including Spain.
 
19. Applications in progress
(The use notified may have been applied for already, or a suitable alternative PPP may be in the process of authorisation. 
Describe such applications, including a possible date of authorisation)
 
The application for the emergency authorization is an extension of an already authorized use of the product in cherry trees granted 
as a minor use authorized in accordance with national regulations.
 
20. Research activities
(Describe the research efforts undertaken and/or in progress, their aims, their funding, and their expected date of results. This is 
needed for all categories of dangers, except quarantine pests that can still be eliminated, or infrequent pests, for which no official 
application for a normal authorisation or extension of use of the plant protection product exists. In case of a repeated 
notification: indicate the state of works of the research projects.)
 
None.

RESOLUCIÓN DE AUTORIZACIÓN EXCEPCIONAL PARA LA APLICACIÓN EN 
POSTCOSECHA DE LOS PRODUCTOS FITOSANITARIOS FORMULADOS A BASE DE 
HEXITIAZOX 10%  [WP] P/P Y HEXITIAZOX 24%  [SC] P/V COMO INSECTICIDAS 
CONTRA TETRANYCHUS SPP. EN EL CULTIVO DEL CEREZO 
 
ANTECEDENTES 
 
La plaga de Tetranychus urticae en cerezo es habitual en las condiciones 
climatológicas de cultivo del Valle del Jerte. 
  
El ataque de esta plaga provoca la defoliación de los árboles e impide la acumulación 
de reservas necesarias para la campaña siguiente, poniendo en riesgo la supervivencia de 
los árboles por la ausencia de masa foliar.  
 
Los formulados Hexitiazox 25.87% (SC) P/V y el Hexitiazox 10% [WP] P/P están 
autorizados en el cultivo de cerezo hasta final de la floración o caída de pétalos, momento 
en el que por las condiciones meteorológicas (bajas temperaturas, alta humedad) no hay 
riesgo de aparición y proliferación de la plaga del ácaro.  El uso de estos dos formulados en 
postcosecha, sería un momento más apropiado, evitando el daño sobre el árbol, ya que las 
condiciones meteorológicas en este estado fenológico, son más propicias para el desarrollo 
de los ácaros.   
 
Es por lo dicho anteriormente por lo que las Comunidades autónomas indicadas en 
el anexo adjunto, desde sus correspondientes Direcciones Generales, han solicitado la 
autorización excepcional para la aplicación en postcosecha de los productos fitosanitarios 
formulados a base de hexitiazox 10% [WP] P/P y hexitiazox 24% [SC] P/V como insecticidas 
contra Tetranychus spp. en el cultivo del cerezo. 
 
 
FUNDAMENTOS DE DERECHO 
 
I.- Que esta Dirección General es competente para la resolución de la solicitud, de 
conformidad con lo previsto en el artículo 7 del Real Decreto 971/2014, de 21 de noviembre, 
por el que se regula el procedimiento de evaluación de productos fitosanitarios, en relación 
con el artículo 4 del Real Decreto 717/2024, de 23 de julio, por el que se desarrolla la 
estructura orgánica básica del Ministerio de Agricultura, Pesca y Alimentación. 
 
II.- Que el artículo 53 del Reglamento (CE) nº 1107/2009 del Parlamento Europeo y del 
Consejo, de 20 de octubre de 2009, relativo a la comercialización de productos fitosanitarios 
y por el que se derogan las Directivas 79/117/CEE y 91/414/CEE del Consejo establece que, 
en circunstancias especiales, un Estado miembro podría autorizar, por un periodo no 
superior a 120 días, la comercialización de productos fitosanitarios para su utilización 
controlada y limitada, si tal medida fuera necesaria debido a un peligro que no pueda 
controlarse por otros medios razonables. 
 
III.- Que el artículo 34 de la Ley 43/2002, de 20 de noviembre, de sanidad vegetal, establece 
la posibilidad de que el Ministerio de Agricultura, Pesca y Alimentación conceda 
autorizaciones excepcionales de un producto fitosanitario en caso de peligro imprevisible 
que no pueda ser controlado por otros medios.

Por todo lo expuesto y, ante la excepcionalidad de la situación, RESUELVO: 
 
PRIMERO.- Autorizar excepcionalmente la aplicación en postcosecha de los productos 
fitosanitarios formulados autorizados en cerezo en el Registro Oficial de Productos 
Fitosanitarios del MAPA a base de Hexitiazox 10% [WP] P/P y Hexitiazox 24% [SC] P/V 
como insecticidas contra Tetranychus spp., en las condiciones y Comunidades autónomas 
que se indican en el anexo adjunto y únicamente por el plazo establecido en el punto 
segundo. 
 
SEGUNDO.- La autorización tendrá efecto a partir del 9 de junio a 28 de septiembre de 2026. 
 
TERCERO.- Los tratamientos deberán ser efectuados por agricultores y aplicadores 
profesionales, bajo el control de las autoridades competentes de la Comunidad autónoma. 
 
CUMPLASE Y NOTIFIQUESE a las Comunidades autónomas y titulares de los formulados 
y dese traslado a la Comisión Europea, conforme al artículo 53 del Reglamento (CE) nº 
1107/2009. 
 
 
La presente resolución no agota la vía administrativa, y contra ella podrá recurrirse, 
en alzada, ante el Sr. Secretario General de Agricultura y Alimentación, en el plazo de un 
mes, contado a partir del día siguiente a aquel en que tenga lugar su notificación, de acuerdo 
a lo establecido en los artículos 121 y concordantes de la Ley 39/2015, de 1 de octubre, del 
Procedimiento Administrativo Común de las Administraciones Públicas.

to September 15, 2026, inclusive.
 
11. Value of tMRL if needed, including information on the measures taken in order to confine the commodities resulting from 
the treated crop to the territory of the notifying MS pending the setting of a tMRL on the EU level. (PRIMO EFSA model to be 
attached)

 
Not applicable
 
12. Validated analytical method for monitoring of residues in plants and plant products.
 
The method has been submitted to the registration authorities in the European Union: 'GIRPA Study Code: B13-M1-A-01 
(Sponsor Code R-33645)', along with its appendices.
 
13. Function of the product
(E.g. systemic long acting insecticide; foliar fungicide, used for regular control, elimination scenario etc)
 
insecticide
 
14. Type of danger to plant production or ecosystem
(Provide reasoning for what category the 120 day authorisation is given: quarantine pest; emergent pest, either invading non-
native, or native; emerging resistance in a pest, etc. Whereas reference to the EU quarantine legislation may suffice for 
quarantine pests elaborate reasoning should be provided for the category 'any harmful pest')
 
Pistachio: Emergent pest in new growing area, no natural enemies well established, IPM non-chemical practices not sufficient, 
practically no plant protection approved for these uses. Hazelnut tree and walnut tree: Pest damage has shown a consistent 
increase over the years. No effective natural enemies have been established. Current IPM non-chemical strategies are insufficient, 
and there are virtually no approved plant protection products for these specific uses.
 
15. Size and effect of danger
(Describe shortly the area affected, the development over time of the infestation, and the agronomic and economic effects it has)
 
The impact of these pests is expected to increase in the future, affecting the entire Autonomous Community, due to the continuous 
expansion of the area dedicated to these trees in the region.
 
16. Absence of any other reasonable means
(Describe the alternative control measures (chemical, non-chemical and cultural) and indicate why they do not (in combination) 
suffice. Describe which, if any, authorisations for the pest to be controlled exist in other Member States.
 
Integrated pest management methods have proven insufficient to limit damage to plantations in past seasons. Regarding the use of 
plant protection products, currently there is either one or no authorized product available for these pests, and they have proven 
inadequate for pest control in previous years." See detailed report
 
17. Rationale
(Reason the risk management decision based on the findings of 15 to 18, containing especially a description of measures taken to 
ensure consumer protection).
 
We consider that the impact of these pests will increase in the future due to: - The continuous expansion of the area dedicated to 
pistachio cultivation in the region. - The lack of currently authorized and effective control methods. - The limitations of integrated 
pest management (IPM) strategies, which have proven insufficient in previous seasons. The use is limited to one treatment per 
season, with no additional control measures required beyond those already established for any plant protection treatment. 
Pistachio: Use conditions are comparable to those of major crops of reference (pome fruits and stone fruits), and pistachio is a nut 
crop, what reduces risk as shell is not edible. Hazelnut tree and walnut tree: Use conditions are comparable to those of major crops 
of reference (pome fruits and stone fruits), and nut crops have lower dietary risk
 
18. Mitigation measures
(Describe what mitigation measures are taken if needed for minimising risk to humans, animals, and the environment, attach 
summary risk assessment. Describe what measures are taken to limit and control use)
 
Not applicable. This is an authorized product for which a minor use authorization is being requested.

 
19. Applications in progress
(The use notified may have been applied for already, or a suitable alternative PPP may be in the process of authorisation. 
Describe such applications, including a possible date of authorisation)
 
Article 43: The product is authorized in Spain (ES-00629) and is currently undergoing renewal (zRMS Italy).The Spanish 
procedure does not allow for a label extension before this process is completed. Article 33: The company has submitted a new 
dossier to obtain a label extension for tree nuts, with approval not expected during 2025. Therefore, and until the label can be 
extended, it is necessary to grant an emergency authorization
 
20. Research activities
(Describe the research efforts undertaken and/or in progress, their aims, their funding, and their expected date of results. This is 
needed for all categories of dangers, except quarantine pests that can still be eliminated, or infrequent pests, for which no official 
application for a normal authorisation or extension of use of the plant protection product exists. In case of a repeated 
notification: indicate the state of works of the research projects.)
 
Collaboration with regional research centers for the sustainable use of all available solutions

DIRECCIÓN GENERAL DE SANIDAD DE LA

C/ ALMAGRO, 33

Tf no.: 91 347 82 74 
 
RESOLUCIÓN DE AUTORIZACIÓN EXCEPCIONAL PARA LA COMERCIALIZACIÓN Y EL 
USO DE LOS PRODUCTOS FITOSANITARIOS FORMULADOS A BASE DE 
ACETAMIPRID 20%  [SL] P/V PARA EL CONTROL DE Halyomorpha halys Y OTROS 
CHINCHES EN LOS CULTIVOS DE AVELLANO Y NOGAL 
 
ANTECEDENTES 
 
Los daños por plagas de chinches han aumentado de forma constante a lo largo de 
los últimos años en los cultivos de avellano y nogal.  
 
La problemática existente es que no se han establecido enemigos naturales eficaces 
contra estas plagas y los actuales métodos de lucha que se disponen no son suficientemente 
eficaces para su control en sus diferentes estados de desarrollo. 
 
Por todo lo dicho anteriormente, las Comunidades autónomas indicadas en el anex o 
adjunto, desde sus Direcciones Generales correspondientes, han solicitado la autorización 
excepcional para la comercialización y el uso de los productos fitosanitarios formulados a base 
de acetamiprid 20% [SL] P/V para el control de Halyomorpha halys y otros chinches en los 
cultivos de avellano y nogal. 
 
FUNDAMENTOS DE DERECHO 
 
I.- Que esta Dirección General es competente para la resolución de la solicitud, de 
conformidad con lo previsto en el artículo 7 del Real Decreto 971/2014, de 21 de noviembre, 
por el que se regula el procedimiento de evaluación de productos fitosanitarios, en relación 
con el artículo 4 del Real Decreto 717/2024, de 23 de julio, por el que se desarrolla la 
estructura orgánica básica del Ministerio de Agricultura, Pesca y Alimentación. 
 
II.- Que el artículo 53 del Reglamento (CE) nº 1107/2009 del Parlamento Europeo y del 
Consejo, de 20 de octubre de 2009, relativo a la comercialización de productos fitosanitarios 
y por el que se derogan las Directivas 79/117/CEE y 91/414/CEE del Consejo establece que, 
en circunstancias especiales, un Estado miembro podría autorizar, por un periodo no superior 
a 120 días, la comercialización de productos fitosanitarios para su utilización controlada y 
limitada, si tal medida fuera necesaria debido a un peligro que no pueda controlarse por otros 
medios razonables. 
 
III.- Que el artículo 34 de la Ley 43/2002, de 20 de noviembre, de sanidad vegetal, establece 
la posibilidad de que el Ministerio de Agricultura, Pesca y Alimentación conceda 
autorizaciones excepcionales de un producto fitosanitario en caso de peligro imprevisible que 
no pueda ser controlado por otros medios.  
 
Por todo lo expuesto y, ante la excepcionalidad de la situación, RESUELVO: 
 
PRIMERO.- Autorizar excepcionalmente la comercialización y el uso de los productos

Notification of an Emergency Authorisation
 
1. Member State, and MS notification number
 
ES - ES-2026-1
 
2. In case of repeated derogation: no. of previous derogation(s)
 
 
3. Names of active substances
 
tau-Fluvalinate 240.0 g/l
 
4. Trade name of Plant Protection Product
 
KLARTAN EW MAVRIK KLARTAN 24 AF
 
5. Formulation type
 
EW - Emulsion, oil in water
 
6. Authorisation holder
 
Dirección General de Ordenación Agropecuaria de la Junta de Comunidades de Castilla La Mancha
 
7. Time period for authorisation
 
2026-03-19 - 2026-06-14
 
8. Area permitted to be treated
 
 
9. Area actually treated
 
 
10. Further limitations
 
Autonomous Community of Extremadura Authorisation period: from 2026/04/09 to 2026/06/30.
 
11. Value of tMRL if needed, including information on the measures taken in order to confine the commodities resulting from 
the treated crop to the territory of the notifying MS pending the setting of a tMRL on the EU level. (PRIMO EFSA model to be 
attached)
 
Not necessary, compliance with the current MRLs can be proved.
 
12. Validated analytical method for monitoring of residues in plants and plant products.
 

tMRL is not needed.
 
13. Function of the product
(E.g. systemic long acting insecticide; foliar fungicide, used for regular control, elimination scenario etc)
 
insecticide
 
14. Type of danger to plant production or ecosystem
(Provide reasoning for what category the 120 day authorisation is given: quarantine pest; emergent pest, either invading non-
native, or native; emerging resistance in a pest, etc. Whereas reference to the EU quarantine legislation may suffice for 
quarantine pests elaborate reasoning should be provided for the category 'any harmful pest')
 
Eurytoma amygdali (almond wasp), a pest first detected in Spain in 2010, has increased its incidence in recent years. This is 
primarily because part of its life cycle occurs protected inside the fruit, making it difficult for treatments to target anything other 
than the adult population. Furthermore, there are currently no effective pheromone-based or biological control methods available 
for this pest, being necessary the use of agrochemicals.
 
15. Size and effect of danger
(Describe shortly the area affected, the development over time of the infestation, and the agronomic and economic effects it has)
 
Eurytoma causes damage from March to April, before adult emergence. Females begin laying eggs inside newly set fruits. The 
larvae feed on the kernel, leaving empty fruits containing a pupa that will emerge the following spring, thereby prolonging and 
spreading the problem. Without effective control measures, Eurytoma can cause yield losses of up to 90% of the total harvest, 
with a major negative impact on almond producers. This pest was first identified in Albacete in 2010. It is currently a significant 
problem in Murcia and the Valencian Community, and in recent years it has increasingly affected Catalonia, Aragon, and 
Andalusia. It is estimated that 25% of the total almond-growing area is affected by this pest. Almond is a key crop in Spain, with 
more than 760,000 ha cultivated, meaning that approximately 200,000 ha are at risk. No adverse consequences are expected from 
the emergency authorisation application because Tau-fluvalinate 240 g/l was registered in Almonds up to 2018 in Almonds 
without any negative notification.
 
16. Absence of any other reasonable means
(Describe the alternative control measures (chemical, non-chemical and cultural) and indicate why they do not (in combination) 
suffice. Describe which, if any, authorisations for the pest to be controlled exist in other Member States.
 
• Currently, the following active substances are registered in Spain for the control of Eurytoma: paraffinic oil, natural pyrethrins 
and lambda-cyhalothrin. • Paraffinic oil does not provide sufficient efficacy to control pests with mobile adults. Natural pyrethrins 
and lambda-cyhalothrin are hazardous to bees and other pollinators due to their high mortality effects. Therefore, most formulated 
products in this group are subject to restrictions and cannot be applied during the flowering of weeds or crops. In addition, some 
of them have a high potential to induce mite outbreaks. • Cultural methods, the use of pheromones and biological control have not 
demonstrated sufficient efficacy to protect almonds. • This spring has been rainy, and it will not be possible to treat the pest with 
registered products while maintaining a balanced bee population, which would cause serious economic losses in both crop 
pollination and the honey-production sector. • Tau-fluvalinate 240 g/L shows unique compatibility with pollinators due to the 
ability of bees to metabolize this molecule. Tau-fluvalinate is used in beehives to protect against Varroa destructor without 
harmful effects on bees. In addition, studies show that tau-fluvalinate allows populations of key beneficial organisms to recover 
within a few days (3–5 days) and provides significant efficacy against mites. • Tau-fluvalinate 240 g/L is registered in Greece 
under the Minor Use procedure under conditions comparable to those requested in this application, and the Portuguese 
Government has granted an emergency authorization for use in almonds in 2026 with these conditions: • Rate: 400 mL/ha • Spray 
volume: 1,000 to 1,500 L/ha • Application method: foliar spray • Number of applications: 2 • Interval between applications: 
minimum 14 days • Timing: BBCH 51–79 • PHI: 30 days
 
17. Rationale
(Reason the risk management decision based on the findings of 15 to 18, containing especially a description of measures taken to 
ensure consumer protection).
 
Empoasca is considered by the almond sector as an emergent pest. Their damages affect mainly to the poor areas of almonds in 
Spain and can reduce the competitiveness of the new modern plantations. The high number of generations cannot be covered with 

the current products registered. Yield losses can result in the range of 15 to 20 %, depending on variety, time, pressure, etc. 
Restrictions and limitations in applying current products due to environmental issues, joined to low efficacy of beneficials, request 
to increase the number of chemical solutions with better eco-toxicological profile. Substitution of some current treatments with 
Tau-fluvalinate 240 g/l would reduce side effects over other pests with less treatments by season and less impact in the 
environment. The authorization will be communicated to the Eurytoma is considered by the almond sector to be a major pest that 
is very difficult to control. Its damage affects all the main almond-growing areas in Spain and can reduce the competitiveness of 
new, modern plantations. The limited availability of products that can be applied in spring with sufficient efficacy and that are 
compatible with bee activity and other pollinators, together with the absence of other effective control methods, makes it 
necessary to increase the range of chemical solutions with a more favourable ecotoxicological profile. Replacing some current 
treatments with tau-fluvalinate 240 g/L would reduce side effects on other pests, require fewer treatments per season, and lower 
environmental impact. The authorization will be communicated to key stakeholders directly and/or through communications by 
the agrochemical companies, which will ensure compliance with the applicable legislation, in particular by using tau-fluvalinate at 
the authorized dose during the 120-day authorization period. Tau-fluvalinate is not listed in Annex IV of Reg 396/2005 but we 
guarantee the compliance with current MRL according to the requested GAP.
 
18. Mitigation measures
(Describe what mitigation measures are taken if needed for minimising risk to humans, animals, and the environment, attach 
summary risk assessment. Describe what measures are taken to limit and control use)
 
OPERATOR SAFETY Operator will use during mixing/loading: chemical protective gloves + C1 or type 6 chemical protective 
clothing + PB3 or PB4 or C3 apron + chemicals product resistant footwear; and during application: chemical protective gloves + 
protective clothing protection level C1 or type 6 + chemical resistant footwear. WORKER SAFETY During re-entry to the crop, 
the worker will wear: C1 chemical protective clothing or work clothing + closed footwear + chemical protective gloves When 
cleaning and maintaining the equipment, the same protective measures will be applied as in mixing/loading and application. Do 
not enter the treated crops until the spray has dried. ENVIROMENTAL SAFETY Spe 3: To protect aquatic organisms, keep an 
untreated buffer zone of 15 m to surface water + use of 95% drift reducing nozzles. Spe 3: To protect non-target arthropods, keep 
an untreated buffer zone of 20 m to the uncultivated area.
 
19. Applications in progress
(The use notified may have been applied for already, or a suitable alternative PPP may be in the process of authorisation. 
Describe such applications, including a possible date of authorisation)
 
The notified use will also be requested in July 2025 as part of a label extension under Art 33 of Reg 1107/2009. The GAP 
requested within this application is the same that will be included in the label extension dossier. This use is also already 
authorized in other South European countries, like Greece.
 
20. Research activities
(Describe the research efforts undertaken and/or in progress, their aims, their funding, and their expected date of results. This is 
needed for all categories of dangers, except quarantine pests that can still be eliminated, or infrequent pests, for which no official 
application for a normal authorisation or extension of use of the plant protection product exists. In case of a repeated 
notification: indicate the state of works of the research projects.)
 
To submit the mentioned label extension under Art 33, a full data package (efficacy, residues…) has been carried out in order to 
support this use.

RESOLUCIÓN DE AUTORIZACIÓN EXCEPCIONAL PARA LA COMERCIALIZACIÓN Y 
EL USO DE PRODUCTOS FITOSANITARIOS FORMULADOS A BASE DE TAU-
FLUVALINATO 24% [EW] P/V PARA EL CONTROL DE Eurytoma amygdali (AVISPILLA 
DEL ALMENDRO) EN ALMENDRO 
 
 
ANTECEDENTES 
 
Eurytoma amygdali (avispilla del almendro), ha aumentado su incidencia en los 
últimos años. Esto se debe principalmente a que parte de su ciclo vital ocurre protegido 
dentro del fruto, haciendo difícil los tratamientos que se dirijan a cualquier otro objetivo que 
no sea la población adulta.  
 
Eurytoma amygdali causa daños de marzo a abril, antes de la emergencia de los 
adultos. Las hembras comienzan a poner huevos dentro de los frutos recién formados. Las 
larvas se alimentan de la semilla, dejando frutos vacíos que contienen una pupa que 
emergerá la primavera siguiente, prolongando y extendiendo así el problema. Sin medidas 
de control efectivas, Eurytoma puede causar pérdidas de rendimiento de hasta el 90% de 
la cosecha total, con un impacto negativo importante en los productores de almendras. 
 
Los productos fitosanitarios autorizados en el Registro, tienen una eficacia 
insuficiente debido a su disponibilidad limitada para  aplicarse en primavera. 
 
Por todo lo dicho anteriormente, las Comunidades autónomas indicadas en el anex o 
adjunto, desde sus Direcciones Generales correspondientes, han solicitado la autorización 
excepcional para la comercialización y el uso de los productos fitosanitarios formulados a 
base de tau-fluvalinato 24% [EW] P/V para el control de Eurytoma amygdali (avispilla del 
almendro) en almendro. 
 
 
FUNDAMENTOS DE DERECHO 
 
I.- Que esta Dirección General es competente para la resolución de la solicitud, de 
conformidad con lo previsto en el artículo 7 del Real Decreto 971/2014, de 21 de noviembre, 
por el que se regula el procedimiento de evaluación de productos fitosanitarios, en relación 
con el artículo 4 del Real Decreto 717/2024, de 23 de julio, por el que se desarrolla la 
estructura orgánica básica del Ministerio de Agricultura, Pesca y Alimentación. 
 
II.- Que el artículo 53 del Reglamento (CE) nº 1107/2009 del Parlamento Europeo y del 
Consejo, de 20 de octubre de 2009, relativo a la comercialización de productos fitosanitarios 
y por el que se derogan las Directivas 79/117/CEE y 91/414/CEE del Consejo establece que, 
en circunstancias especiales, un Estado miembro podría autorizar, por un periodo no 
superior a 120 días, la comercialización de productos fitosanitarios para su utilización 
controlada y limitada, si tal medida fuera necesaria debido a un peligro que no pueda 
controlarse por otros medios razonables. 
 
III.- Que el artículo 34 de la Ley 43/2002, de 20 de noviembre, de sanidad vegetal, establece 
la posibilidad de que el Ministerio de Agricultura, Pesca y Alimentación conceda

fitosanitarios autorizados actualmente en el Registro Oficial de Productos Fitosanitarios del

SEGUNDO.- La autorización tendrá efecto desde el 19 de marzo al 14 de junio de 2026. 
 
TERCERO.- Los tratamientos deberán ser efectuados bajo el control de las autoridades 
competentes de las Comunidades Autónomas. 
 
CUMPLASE Y NOTIFIQUESE a las Comunidades Autónomas y titulares de los formulados 
y dese traslado a la Comisión Europea, conforme al artículo 53 del Reglamento (CE) nº 
1107/2009.

ANEXO 
 
Productos fitosanitarios y condiciones de uso: 
 
- Productos fitosanitarios formulados a base de Tau-fluvalinato 24% [EW] P/V 
autorizados en el Registro Oficial de Productos Fitosanitarios del MAPA para ser usada 
en la Comunidad Autónoma de Castilla La Mancha.  
- Plaga/enfermedad: Eurytoma amygdali (Avispilla del almendro) 
- Aplicación: Pulverización foliar. BCHH: 11-79 
- Número de aplicaciones: 2 aplicación 
- Intervalo entre aplicaciones: 14 días 
- Dosis máxima: 0,4 L producto/ha (0,03-0,05 l/hl) 
- Volumen: 500-1000 l/ha 
- Plazo de seguridad: 14 días 
- Efecto de la autorización: del 19 de marzo al 14 de junio de 2026. 
 
Nota: En la etiqueta se darán las instrucciones específicas para su correcto uso y las 
advertencias sobre incompatibilidad con otros productos fitosanitarios. 
 
SEGURIDAD DEL OPERADOR 
 
Durante la mezcla/carga: guantes protectores químicos +C1 o ropa protectora química tipo 
6 + PB3 o PB4 o delantal C3 + calzado resistente a productos químicos. 
 
Durante la aplicación: guantes protectores químicos + protección de ropa protectora nivel C1 
o tipo 6 + calzado resistente a productos químicos. 
 
SEGURIDAD DEL TRABAJADOR 
 
Durante la reentrada en la cosecha, el trabajador llevará: ropa de trabajo de protección 
química C1 o ropa de trabajo + calzado cerrado + guantes protectores químicos. 
  
Al limpiar y mantener el equipo, se aplicarán las mismas medidas de protección que en la 
mezcla/carga y aplicación. 
 
No entrar en los cultivos tratados hasta que la aplicación se haya secado. 
 
SEGURIDAD MEDIOAMBIENTAL 
 
Spe 3: Para proteger a los organismos acuáticos, mantener una banda de seguridad sin 
tratar de 15 m respecto a las masas de agua superficiales + uso de boquillas reductoras de 
deriva al 95%. 
 
Spe 3: Para proteger a los artrópodos no objetivo, mantener una banda de seguridad sin 
tratar de 20 m hasta la zona no cultivada.

records.fullText:
Notification of an Emergency Authorisation
 
1. Member State, and MS notification number
 
ES - ES-2025-34
 
2. In case of repeated derogation: no. of previous derogation(s)
 
 
3. Names of active substances
 
Acetamiprid 200.0 g/l
 
4. Trade name of Plant Protection Product
 
CARNADINE
 
5. Formulation type
 
SL - Soluble concentrate
 
6. Authorisation holder
 
Dirección General de Ordenación Agropecuaria de la Junta de Comunidades de Castilla La Mancha
 
7. Time period for authorisation
 
2025-06-03 - 2025-07-31
 
8. Area permitted to be treated
 
 
9. Area actually treated
 
 
10. Further limitations
 
Autonomous Community of Castilla La Mancha: Pistachio: entry into force: 2025-06-03, expiry date: 2025-07-31 Autonomous 
Community of Cataluña: Hazel and wallnut: entry into force: 2025-07-17 expiry date: 2025-09-31
 
11. Value of tMRL if needed, including information on the measures taken in order to confine the commodities resulting from 
the treated crop to the territory of the notifying MS pending the setting of a tMRL on the EU level. (PRIMO EFSA model to be 
attached)
 
Not applicable
 
12. Validated analytical method for monitoring of residues in plants and plant products.

 
The method has been submitted to the registration authorities in the European Union: 'GIRPA Study Code: B13-M1-A-01 
(Sponsor Code R-33645)', along with its appendices.
 
13. Function of the product
(E.g. systemic long acting insecticide; foliar fungicide, used for regular control, elimination scenario etc)
 
insecticide
 
14. Type of danger to plant production or ecosystem
(Provide reasoning for what category the 120 day authorisation is given: quarantine pest; emergent pest, either invading non-
native, or native; emerging resistance in a pest, etc. Whereas reference to the EU quarantine legislation may suffice for 
quarantine pests elaborate reasoning should be provided for the category 'any harmful pest')
 
Pistachio: Emergent pest in new growing area, no natural enemies well established, IPM non-chemical practices not sufficient, 
practically no plant protection approved for these uses. Hazelnut tree and walnut tree: Pest damage has shown a consistent 
increase over the years. No effective natural enemies have been established. Current IPM non-chemical strategies are insufficient, 
and there are virtually no approved plant protection products for these specific uses.
 
15. Size and effect of danger
(Describe shortly the area affected, the development over time of the infestation, and the agronomic and economic effects it has)
 
The impact of these pests is expected to increase in the future, affecting the entire Autonomous Community, due to the continuous 
expansion of the area dedicated to these trees in the region.
 
16. Absence of any other reasonable means
(Describe the alternative control measures (chemical, non-chemical and cultural) and indicate why they do not (in combination) 
suffice. Describe which, if any, authorisations for the pest to be controlled exist in other Member States.
 
Integrated pest management methods have proven insufficient to limit damage to plantations in past seasons. Regarding the use of 
plant protection products, currently there is either one or no authorized product available for these pests, and they have proven 
inadequate for pest control in previous years." See detailed report
 
17. Rationale
(Reason the risk management decision based on the findings of 15 to 18, containing especially a description of measures taken to 
ensure consumer protection).
 
We consider that the impact of these pests will increase in the future due to: - The continuous expansion of the area dedicated to 
pistachio cultivation in the region. - The lack of currently authorized and effective control methods. - The limitations of integrated 
pest management (IPM) strategies, which have proven insufficient in previous seasons. The use is limited to one treatment per 
season, with no additional control measures required beyond those already established for any plant protection treatment. 
Pistachio: Use conditions are comparable to those of major crops of reference (pome fruits and stone fruits), and pistachio is a nut 
crop, what reduces risk as shell is not edible. Hazelnut tree and walnut tree: Use conditions are comparable to those of major crops 
of reference (pome fruits and stone fruits), and nut crops have lower dietary risk
 
18. Mitigation measures
(Describe what mitigation measures are taken if needed for minimising risk to humans, animals, and the environment, attach 
summary risk assessment. Describe what measures are taken to limit and control use)
 
Not applicable. This is an authorized product for which a minor use authorization is being requested.
 
19. Applications in progress
(The use notified may have been applied for already, or a suitable alternative PPP may be in the process of authorisation. 
Describe such applications, including a possible date of authorisation)
 

Article 43: The product is authorized in Spain (ES-00629) and is currently undergoing renewal (zRMS Italy).The Spanish 
procedure does not allow for a label extension before this process is completed. Article 33: The company has submitted a new 
dossier to obtain a label extension for tree nuts, with approval not expected during 2025. Therefore, and until the label can be 
extended, it is necessary to grant an emergency authorization
 
20. Research activities
(Describe the research efforts undertaken and/or in progress, their aims, their funding, and their expected date of results. This is 
needed for all categories of dangers, except quarantine pests that can still be eliminated, or infrequent pests, for which no official 
application for a normal authorisation or extension of use of the plant protection product exists. In case of a repeated 
notification: indicate the state of works of the research projects.)
 
Collaboration with regional research centers for the sustainable use of all available solutions

Notification of an Emergency Authorisation

11. Value of tMRL if needed, including information on the measures taken in order to confine the commodities resulting from 
the treated crop to the territory of the notifying MS pending the setting of a tMRL on the EU level. (PRIMO EFSA model to be 
attached)
 
The requested cultivation practice is the same one that is currently authorized. However, the third application subject to 
exceptional authorization may only be made after collection.

 
12. Validated analytical method for monitoring of residues in plants and plant products.
 
It is not necessary
 
13. Function of the product
(E.g. systemic long acting insecticide; foliar fungicide, used for regular control, elimination scenario etc)
 
insecticide
 
14. Type of danger to plant production or ecosystem
(Provide reasoning for what category the 120 day authorisation is given: quarantine pest; emergent pest, either invading non-
native, or native; emerging resistance in a pest, etc. Whereas reference to the EU quarantine legislation may suffice for 
quarantine pests elaborate reasoning should be provided for the category 'any harmful pest')
 
The big-headed worm (Capnodis tenebrionis) is one of the main pests that affects almond, peach and nectarine crops in our 
autonomous community. The biological cycle of this pest makes it necessary to carry out treatments for its control in spring, at 
which time the wintering adults appear, and in summer, at which time the new adults emerge. They cause damage to the leaves 
and shoots, where bites can be observed. On the other hand, it is also necessary to control larvae in spring, they feed on the roots 
causing the weakening of the trees and frequently causing their death.
 
15. Size and effect of danger
(Describe shortly the area affected, the development over time of the infestation, and the agronomic and economic effects it has)
 
The autonomous community of Andalusia is the main producer of almonds nationwide, with a cultivation area of 234,100 ha, 
according to the 2022 Yearbook of Agricultural and Fisheries Statistics, cultivation that is carried out mainly in dry land. 
According to the same source, the area of peach and nectarine crops in the same year was 2,368 ha and 1,584 ha, respectively.
 
16. Absence of any other reasonable means
(Describe the alternative control measures (chemical, non-chemical and cultural) and indicate why they do not (in combination) 
suffice. Describe which, if any, authorisations for the pest to be controlled exist in other Member States.
 
Added to the persistent drought in Andalusia is the absence of systemic phytosanitary products that act by contact and ingestion, 
such as those composed of the active substances imidacloprid or thiacloprid. Consequently, the control of the pest has become 
more difficult. Consulting the Official Register of Phytosanitary Products and Material, it has been verified that at this time it is 
only possible to make two applications of acetamiprid for the control of adults of this pest. As a general rule, one of these 
applications is being used, according to the sector, to control other important pests for these crops, such as aphids. Consequently, 
in practice, only a single application is available to cover the next emergence period of bighead worm adults, which is between 
mid-August and the end of September. On the other hand, indicate that the active substance chlorantraniliprole is also authorized 
for the control of Coleoptera in the indicated crops. However, it presents a limited efficacy in the control of adults, in accordance 
with the test entitled: "Control of Big- headed Worm (Capnodis tenebrionis L.) by means of phytosanitary treatments.", which is 
attached as Annex No. 1. For For its part, the substance acetamiptrid is highly effective in controlling adults of this pest, according 
to the same trial. Likewise, it should be noted that there is no active substance authorized for the control of larvae. Consequently, 
it is only possible to carry out applications for the control of adults, which makes it extremely difficult to control the pest once it is 
installed in the cultivation plot.
 
17. Rationale
(Reason the risk management decision based on the findings of 15 to 18, containing especially a description of measures taken to 
ensure consumer protection).
 
The producing sector, represented by Asociafruit, has expressed to this General Directorate the need to use the active substance 
acetamiprid 20% in a third application for the control of the big- headed worm in peach, nectarine and almond plantations , as the 
only effective means to fight against this plague An exceedance of the current MRL for peach, nectarine and almond is not 
expected. The proposed uses of acetamiprid do not represent unacceptable acute and chronic risks for the consumer.
 

18. Mitigation measures
(Describe what mitigation measures are taken if needed for minimising risk to humans, animals, and the environment, attach 
summary risk assessment. Describe what measures are taken to limit and control use)
 
The requested cultivation practice is the same one that is currently authorized. However, the third application subject to 
exceptional authorization may only be made after collection.
 
19. Applications in progress
(The use notified may have been applied for already, or a suitable alternative PPP may be in the process of authorisation. 
Describe such applications, including a possible date of authorisation)
 
There is no request in progress.
 
20. Research activities
(Describe the research efforts undertaken and/or in progress, their aims, their funding, and their expected date of results. This is 
needed for all categories of dangers, except quarantine pests that can still be eliminated, or infrequent pests, for which no official 
application for a normal authorisation or extension of use of the plant protection product exists. In case of a repeated 
notification: indicate the state of works of the research projects.)

9. Value of tMRL if needed, including information on the measures taken in order to confine the commodities resulting from the
treated crop to the territory of the notifying MS pending the setting of a tMRL on the EU level. (PRIMO EFSA model to be
attached) 
No need for tMRL as submitted residue trials show residues < LOQ for almonds 
10. Validated analytical method for monitoring of residues in plants and plant products. 
With regard to request of the minor use extension to Almond, a validation of the method for the determination of residues is
performed, as tree nuts correspond to high oil content and very low water content commodities according to SANTE/11813/2017
guidance document, and there isn't included in this group any registered use of the product FLASH UM (reg. No.: 19.241). The
aim of this analytical method, was the determination of Fenpyroximate residues in apple, oilseed rape seed, dried broad beans,
wheat grain, whole orange, hops, sugarbeet roots and sugarbeet tops with leaves. Employed method RES/RAM/004 is based on
the QuEChERS (EN 15662:2008) procedure and involves extraction of residues of fenpyroximate and M-1 by agitation with
acetonitrile followed by extract purification prior to final determination by LC-MS/MS. This procedure was found to be valid for
the determination of Fenpyroximate and M-1 residues in apple, oilseed rape seed, dried broad bean, wheat grain, whole orange,
hops, sugarbeet roots and sugarbeet tops and leaves with an LOQ of 0.01 mg/kg. 
11. Function of the product 
(E.g. systemic long acting insecticide; foliar fungicide, used for regular control, elimination scenario etc) 
 insecticide 
12. Type of danger to plant production or ecosystem 
(Provide reasoning for what category the 120 day authorisation is given: quarantine pest; emergent pest, either invading
non-native, or native; emerging resistance in a pest, etc. Whereas reference to the EU quarantine legislation may suffice for
quarantine pests elaborate reasoning should be provided for the category 'any harmful pest') 
Green mosquito (Empoasca decedens) is an emerging pest affecting almonds, being considerèd one of the most relevant. This pest
affects equally from larvae and adults and it produces deformed leaves and growth limitation, with serious problems reported in
the pastfew years in new plantations in Spain. Red spider mites (Panonychus ulml is a pest that feeds from leaves and it
producesdefoliation when strong attacks occur, particularly under dry hot conditions (frequent in the region). For both pests,
limited products are registered cumently in Spain and therefore the limitation of their control. 
13. Size and effect of danger 
(Describe shortly the area affected, the development over time of the infestation, and the agronomic and economic effects it has) 
584,000 ha of Almonds in Spain, 39,000 has iii Catalonia, are affected by pest leading to yield decreases because of the
infestation damages. Green mosquitoes (Empoasca decedens) produce important damage in almonds, particularly in new
plantations. Red spider mites (Panonychus ulmi) produce also defoliation in trees leading to a complete growth stagnation,
seriously jeopardizing almond production. 
14. Absence of any other reasonable means 
(Describe the alternative control measures (chemical, non-chemical and cultural) and indicate why they do not (in combination)
suffice. Describe which, if any, authorisations for the pest to be controlled exist in other Member States. 
There are few chemical products registered in Spain on almonds for both pests. In order to control red spider mites(Panonïchus
ulmi), the active suhstance hexitiazox (10% WP) is registered in Spain. It is a valid substance but it shows limited control, as it is
only effective against larvae and eggs. Adult red spider mite control is not achieved with this active substance. According to the
Spanish Guide of Integrated Pest Management in Almonds, it is very important to iimit the occurrence of motiie forms from the
ärst genoration. It is aiso recommended only applications when 5% of sprouts are already affected. This fact limits the efficacy of
the cunent products registered on Almonds (hexitiazox shows limited control as it only targets larvae and eggs). Additionally,
IRAC has identified the red spider mites (Panonychus ulmi) as a pest with a high intrinsic risk for resistance appearance in Spain
(IRAC SPAIN), therefore the use of different modes of action is vital to maintain high efficacy in the control of this pest. There
are other two products registered for the control of red spider mites (Panonychus ulmi). Sulfur is one of them, but it is widely
 
Generated by PPPAMS - Published on 09/12/2019 - Page 2 of 5

recognized its low efficacy. The other one is lime sulphur (calcium polysulphid). This product is not useful hecause it has limited
applications: only before flowering and only when the previous season the almonds suffered a strong attack of red spider mites.
For green mosquito (Empoasca decedens), only two active substances are registered in Spain: Azadirachtin (3.2% EC) and
tau-fluvalinate (lYo EW and 24% SC). This synthetic pyrethroid is the only specific product for green mosquito control. Different
modes of action and chemical families are requested for a correct integrates pest management and for green mosquito only this
specific insecticide is registered. In this scene there are not enough PPP to control these pests in a sustainable way. 
15. Rationale 
(Reason the risk management decision based on the findings of 15 to 18, containing especially a description of measures taken to
ensure consumer protection). 
Considering that: - the product is currently registered in Spain on a number of uses/crops, - the label extension of Fenpyroximate
5.12% w/v SC on Almond as it is mentioned in the application to the Spanish Ministry of Agriculture does not imply a
considerable risk to consumer. - All assessments performed on the product have supported the lack of PHI for the use of
Fenpyroximate 5.12% w/v SC on Almond. the measures to ensure consumer protection are consistent with the authorisation of
Fenpyroximate 5.12% w/v SC on Almond. 
16. Mitigation measures 
(Describe what mitigation measures are taken if needed for minimising risk to humans, animals, and the environment, attach
summary risk assessment. Describe what measures are taken to limit and control use) 
It is considered that there is no need to submit environmentalfate and behaviour data nor ecotoxicological data for the use of the
product FLASH UM (reg. No.: 19,241) to Almond as the product is authorized on Peach with the same proposed GAP that the one
proposed for Almond. Therefore, the same mitigation measures that are cunently applied for Peach will be eligible for Almond. 
17. Applications in progress 
(The use notified may have been applied for already, or a suitable alternative PPP may be in the process of authorisation. Describe
such applications, including a possible date of authorisation) 
Sipcam Inagra S.A. has recently applied for the label extension for FLASH UM (fenpyroximate 5.12% w/v SC) for almonds under
the procedure of minor uses for national authorisation in Spain (according to Article 51 of Regulation (EC) No. 1107/2009). Its
completeness check was obtained the date 05/March/2018. 
18. Research activities 
(Describe the research efforts undertaken and/or in progress, their aims, their funding, and their expected date of results. This is
needed for all categories of dangers, except quarantine pests that can still be eliminated, or infrequent pests, for which no official
application for a normal authorisation or extension of use of the plant protection product exists. In case of a repeated notification:
indicate the state of works of the research projects.) 
The product FLASH UM is curently registered in Spain and it has been of interest for several growers associations (including
almond growers, strawberry growers and tomato growers). Recently, Sipcam performed several trials in order to determine the
effect of FLASH UM on beneficials and it has been accepted under the Integrated Pest Management Schemes of several
autonomous communities (regional governments). FLASH UM authorisation has been granted in Spain until 30/April/2020,
following the Regulation (EC) No. 1107/2009 (and not the Dir. 91/414/EEC any more).

SEGURIDAD ALIMENTARIA 
RESOLUCIÓN DE AUTORIZACIÓN EXCEPCIONAL PARA LA COMERCIALIZACIÓN Y 
EL   USO   DE   LOS   PRODUCTOS   FITOSANITARIOS   FORMULADOS   A   BASE   DE 
ACETAMIPRID 20% [SG] P/P PARA EL CONTROL DE GUSANO CABEZUDO   EN LOS 
CULTIVOS DEL MELOCOTONERO, NECTARINO Y ALMENDRO 
ANTECEDENTES 
El gusano cabezudo ( Capnodis tenebrionis ) es una de las principales plagas que 
afecta a los cultivos del almendro, melocotonero y nectarino. El ciclo biológico de esta plaga 
hace neces ario la realización de tratamientos para su control en primavera, momento en el 
cual aparecen los adultos invernantes, y en verano, momento en el que emergen los nuevos 
adultos. Los adultos provocan daños en las hojas y brotes, donde se pueden observar 
mor deduras. Las larvas se alimentan de las raíces causando el debilitamiento de los árboles 
y provocando con frecuencia la muerte de los mismos. 
La incidencia de la plaga es mayor en plantaciones de secano, ya que la humedad 
del suelo actúa como un factor li mitante al provocar la muerte de los huevos y de las larvas 
neonatas. Las altas temperaturas registradas en las últimas semanas han provocado una 
rápida evaporación de la humedad acumulada en el suelo. Estas condiciones, crean un 
ambiente especialmente fav orable para el desarrollo y proliferación de la plaga, cuyas larvas 
permanecen   activas en el interior de las raíces, protegidas de las condiciones superficiales. 
A lo dicho anteriormente, se s uma la   falta   de productos fitosanitarios   registrados 
sistémico s con acción por contacto e ingestión . 
Por todo lo dicho anteriormente, las Comunidades autónomas indicadas en el anexo 
adjunto, desde sus Direcciones Generales correspondientes, han solicitado la autorización 
excepcional   de   una   tercera   aplicación   post   co secha   de   los   productos   fitosanitarios 
autorizados en el Registro Oficial de Productos Fitosanitarios, formulados a base de 
acetamiprid 20% [SG] P/P que están autorizados   en el melocotonero   ( se incluye   nectarino ) 
o   almendro. 
FUNDAME NTOS DE DERECHO 
I. -   Que esta Dirección General es competente para la resolución de la solicitud, de 
conformidad con lo previsto en el artículo 7 del Real Decreto 971/2014, de 21 de noviembre, 
por el que se regula el procedimiento de evaluación de   productos fitosanitarios, en relación 
con el artículo 4 del Real Decreto 717/2024, de 23 de julio, por el que se desarrolla la 
estructura orgánica básica del Ministerio de Agricultura, Pesca y Alimentación. 
II. -   Que el artículo 53   del Reglamento (CE) nº 1107/2009   del Parlamento Europeo y del 
Consejo, de 20 de octubre de 2009, relativo a la comercialización de productos fitosanitarios 
y por el que se derogan las Directivas 79/117/CEE y 91/414/CEE del Consejo establece que, 
en circun stancias especiales, un Estado miembro podría autorizar, por un periodo no 
superior a 120 días, la comercialización de productos fitosanitarios para su utilización 
controlada y limitada, si tal medida fuera necesaria debido a un peligro que no pueda 
contro larse por otros medios razonables.

III. -   Que el artículo 34 de la Ley 43/2002, de 20 de noviembre, de sanidad vegetal, establece 
la   posibilidad   de   que   el   Ministerio   de   Agricultura,   Pesca   y   Alimentación   conceda 
autorizaciones excepcionales de un producto f itosanitario en caso de peligro imprevisible 
que no pueda ser controlado por otros medios. 
Por todo lo expuesto y, ante la excepcionalidad de la situación,   RESUELVO: 
PRIMERO. -   Autorizar excepcionalmente   los productos fitosanitarios   formulados a base de 
acetamiprid 20% [SG] P/P   autorizados en el Registro   Oficial de Productos Fitosanitarios del 
MAPA   en mel ocotonero (incluye nectarino)   o   almendro   una tercera aplicación   para su uso 
contra gusano cabezudo,   en las condiciones y Comunidades autónomas que se ind ican en 
el anexo adjunto y únicamente por el plazo establecido en el punto segundo, para una 
utilización controlada y limitada. 
SEGUNDO. -   La autorización tendrá vigencia desde el   15 de julio hasta el 11   de   noviembre 
de 2026 . 
TERCERO. -   Los tratamientos   deberán ser efectuados bajo el control de las autoridades 
competentes de las Comunidades autónomas indicadas en el Anexo adjunto. Además, esta 
autoridad, deberá establecer mecanismos de inspección, vigilancia, control y sanción con el 
fin de asegurar una r educción al mínimo de los posibles riesgos que puedan surgir como 
consecuencia de la aplicación de los productos fitosanitarios autorizados. 
CUMPLASE Y NOTIFIQUESE   a las Comunidades autónomas y a los titulares de los 
formulados referenciados y dese trasla do a la Comisión Europea, conforme al artículo 53 del 
Reglamento (CE) nº 1107/2009. 
La presente resolución no agota la vía administrativa, y contra ella podrá recurrirse, en 
alzada, ante el Sr. Secretario General de Agricultura y Alimentación, en el plaz o de un mes, 
contado a partir del día siguiente a aquel en que tenga lugar su notificación ,   de acuerdo a lo 
establecido en los artículos 121 y concordantes de la Ley 39/2015, de 1 de octubre, del 
Procedimiento Administrativo Común de las Administraciones P úblicas. 
Firmado electrónicamente por, 
EL DIRECTOR GENERAL 
Emilio Luis García Muro
